results.name: early_session_yes_gap
results.description: Yes rate on trials with trial_index < 118 (first quarter of the session) minus yes rate on later trials; observed < null means people start out more conservative than later in the session, a warm-up drift the stationary model cannot produce (observed > null: they start more liberal).

results.name: n4_vs_n3_parity_match_yes
results.description: Among sets whose examples all share one parity, yes rate for parity-matching non-member targets on four-example sets minus that on three-example sets; observed < null means people narrow generalization from 3 to 4 examples more than the memory-drop model allows (observed > null: the model narrows too much at four examples).
results.code:
# name: n4_vs_n3_parity_match_yes
# description: Among sets whose examples all share one parity, yes rate for parity-matching non-member targets on four-example sets minus that on three-example sets; observed < null means people narrow generalization from 3 to 4 examples more than the memory-drop model allows (observed > null: the model narrows too much at four examples).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    u, inv = np.unique(sets, return_inverse=True)
    ex = [[int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u]
    nn = np.array([len(e) for e in ex])
    par = np.array([e[0] % 2 if len({x % 2 for x in e}) == 1 else -1 for e in ex])
    mem = np.zeros((len(u), 101), bool)
    for i, e in enumerate(ex):
        mem[i, e] = True
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    ok = (par[inv] >= 0) & (t % 2 == par[inv]) & ~mem[inv, t]
    a = ok & (nn[inv] == 4)
    b = ok & (nn[inv] == 3)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: progression_extrapolation_gap
results.description: On 2-4-example sets whose sorted examples form an arithmetic progression, among targets outside the examples' range, yes rate for targets continuing the step (e.g. 12 or 42 for 62,32,22) minus yes rate for other out-of-range targets; observed > null means people extrapolate the step pattern beyond the examples more sharply than the model (observed < null: the model over-extrapolates the progression).
results.code:
# name: progression_extrapolation_gap
# description: On 2-4-example sets whose sorted examples form an arithmetic progression, among targets outside the examples' range, yes rate for targets continuing the step (e.g. 12 or 42 for 62,32,22) minus yes rate for other out-of-range targets; observed > null means people extrapolate the step pattern beyond the examples more sharply than the model (observed < null: the model over-extrapolates the progression).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    u, inv = np.unique(sets, return_inverse=True)
    K = len(u)
    lo = np.zeros(K); hi = np.zeros(K); step = np.zeros(K, int); prog = np.zeros(K, bool)
    for i, s in enumerate(u):
        e = sorted(int(x) for x in s.split(","))
        lo[i], hi[i] = e[0], e[-1]
        if len(e) >= 2:
            g = e[1] - e[0]
            if g > 0 and all(e[j + 1] - e[j] == g for j in range(len(e) - 1)):
                prog[i] = True
                step[i] = g
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    st = np.maximum(step[inv], 1)
    hit = prog[inv] & ((t - lo[inv]) % st == 0) & (np.abs(t - lo[inv]) % st == 0)
    out = hit & ((t < lo[inv]) | (t > hi[inv]))
    outr = prog[inv] & ((t < lo[inv]) | (t > hi[inv]))
    inside = outr & ~hit
    if out.sum() == 0 or inside.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[out].mean() - r[inside].mean())

results.name: n4_set_mean_variance
results.description: Variance across four-example sets of each set's mean yes rate; observed > null means people's breadth of generalization differs more between four-example sets than the memory-drop model predicts (observed < null: the model over-differentiates four-example sets).

results.name: same_half_magnitude_gap
results.description: On 2-4-example sets whose examples all lie in one half of 1-100 (all <=50 or all >50), yes rate for targets in that same half minus targets in the other half; observed > null means people treat 'small numbers'/'big numbers' as a category more sharply than the model's distance band (observed < null: the model over-sharpens magnitude).

results.name: multi_common_divisor_gap
results.description: On 2-4-example sets, yes rate for non-member targets >=2 that divide every example (e.g. 15 for 90,45) minus yes rate for other non-member targets on those same kinds of sets; observed > null means people generalize downward to common divisors more than the model (whose properties only look at what the examples are multiples of), observed < null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: multi_common_divisor_gap
# description: On 2-4-example sets, yes rate for non-member targets >=2 that divide every example (e.g. 15 for 90,45) minus yes rate for other non-member targets on those same kinds of sets; observed > null means people generalize downward to common divisors more than the model (whose properties only look at what the examples are multiples of), observed < null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    u, inv = np.unique(sets, return_inverse=True)
    ex = [[int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    T = np.arange(101)
    divm = np.zeros((len(u), 101), bool)
    mem = np.zeros((len(u), 101), bool)
    multi = np.zeros(len(u), bool)
    for i, e in enumerate(ex):
        multi[i] = len(e) >= 2
        dv = np.ones(101, bool)
        for x in e:
            dv &= (T >= 2) & (x % np.maximum(T, 1) == 0)
            mem[i, x] = True
        divm[i] = dv
    isdiv = divm[inv, t]
    ism = mem[inv, t]
    m = multi[inv] & ~ism
    a, b = m & isdiv, m & ~isdiv
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: multi_multiple_of_max_gap
results.description: On 2-4-example sets, yes rate for non-member targets that are multiples of the largest example (e.g. 64 for 8,32; 96 for 16,32,2,8) minus yes rate for other non-member targets; observed > null means people extend a scaling/multiplicative rule upward beyond what the model's shared-property profile predicts (observed < null: model over-extends).
results.code:
# name: multi_multiple_of_max_gap
# description: On 2-4-example sets, yes rate for non-member targets that are multiples of the largest example (e.g. 64 for 8,32; 96 for 16,32,2,8) minus yes rate for other non-member targets; observed > null means people extend a scaling/multiplicative rule upward beyond what the model's shared-property profile predicts (observed < null: model over-extends).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    u, inv = np.unique(sets, return_inverse=True)
    ex = [[int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u]
    mx = np.array([max(e) for e in ex])
    nn = np.array([len(e) for e in ex])
    mem = np.zeros((len(u), 101), bool)
    for i, e in enumerate(ex):
        mem[i, e] = True
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    m = (nn[inv] >= 2) & ~mem[inv, t]
    hit = (t % mx[inv]) == 0
    a, b = m & hit, m & ~hit
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: multi_outside_span_far_near_gap
results.description: On 2-4-example sets, yes rate for targets far outside the examples' range (more than 30 beyond the nearest end) minus targets just outside (1-10 beyond); observed > null means people's endorsement falls off with distance outside the range less steeply than the model's Gaussian band (observed < null: falls off more steeply).
results.code:
# name: multi_outside_span_far_near_gap
# description: On 2-4-example sets, yes rate for targets far outside the examples' range (more than 30 beyond the nearest end) minus targets just outside (1-10 beyond); observed > null means people's endorsement falls off with distance outside the range less steeply than the model's Gaussian band (observed < null: falls off more steeply).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    u, inv = np.unique(sets, return_inverse=True)
    lo = np.array([min(int(x) for x in s.split(",")) for s in u])
    hi = np.array([max(int(x) for x in s.split(",")) for s in u])
    nn = np.array([s.count(",") + 1 for s in u])
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    gap = np.maximum(0, np.maximum(lo[inv] - t, t - hi[inv]))
    m = nn[inv] >= 2
    far = m & (gap > 30)
    near = m & (gap >= 1) & (gap <= 10)
    if far.sum() == 0 or near.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[far].mean() - r[near].mean())
